To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) ASV-30 is a potent and selective CRF(1)-receptor antagonist that reduces anxiety-like behavior in mice; 2) the CRF(1/2)-receptor antagonist astressin reduces anxiety-like behavior and blunts the ACTH response; and 3) the new selective CRFR2 agonist urocorticin-II increases anxiety-like behavior in a dose-dependent manner in the elevated plus maze test.
the CRF2 receptor is involved in the behavioral but not the endocrine response to stress.
the CRF-2 receptor plays a role primarily in behavioral, but also in some physiological responses to stress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the central corticotropins releasing factor(2) (CRF(2)) receptor in the behavioral response to environmental stressors.
the role of CRF and the CRF(1 and 2) receptors in the behavioral and neuroendocrine responses to environmental stress.
the role of CRF in the behavioral, endocrine, and autonomic responses to stress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CRF(2), in contrast to CRF(1), plays a role in stress- and anxiety-related behavior, but not in the stress response.
the CRF2 receptor subtype is involved in the behavioral, and not the neuroendocrine, response to stress.
CRF(1), CRF(2), and urocortin receptors are all important in the behavioral and neuroendocrine response to stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CRF(2)-mediated signaling may be important in the modulation of anxiety-like behavior, but not the ACTH response, in the stress response to stress.
CRF(1)- and CRF( 2)-receptor antagonists may be useful in the treatment of stress-related disorders, but that CRF(2)-receptor agonists may be useful for the treatment of anxiety.
CRF(1)-receptors are responsible for stress-induced ACTH release, whereas CRF(2)-receptors are involved in stress-related anxiety.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the behavioral response to stress is not mediated by the same neural circuitry as the endocrine response to stress.
the CRF receptor system plays a role in behavioral, but probably not endocrine, responses to stress.
the CRF system is a very complex one.
